item.title: Merck Sacituzumab (Sac-TMT) Wins
item.description:
• Summary: Merck and its partner Kelun-Biotech announced a pivotal Phase 3 win for Sac-TMT (sacituzumab tirumotecan) in endometrial cancer, marking the first global Phase 3 success for this Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). The trial met its primary endpoint ahead of schedule, supporting regulatory submissions. Sac-TMT is part of a burgeoning class of ADCs targeting Trop-2, which includes Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan). The positive data reinforce the potential of this ADC in endometrial cancer, an area with limited treatment options.
  • MoAs: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (Trop-2); delivers a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumor cells.
  • Sources: ApexOnco, Fierce Pharma, BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News

item.title: EHA 2026 Preview: Bristol's Celmod
item.description:
• Summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb is set to present clinical data for its novel cereblon E3 ligase modulator (Celmod) at the EHA 2026 congress. The preview highlights the agent's potential in hematologic malignancies, building on the company's expertise in immunomodulatory drugs (IMiDs) and CELMoDs. Specific trial details were not disclosed in the single article.
  • MoAs: Cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD); induces ubiquitin‑mediated degradation of transcription factors Ikaros (IKZF1) and Aiolos (IKZF3), leading to anti‑myeloma and anti‑lymphoma activity.
  • Sources: ApexOnco

item.title: Enhertu Early Breast Cancer Approvals
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA granted dual approvals for Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan, Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca) in early breast cancer. The approvals expand the use of this HER2‑directed antibody‑drug conjugate to earlier lines of therapy, potentially changing treatment paradigms for HER2‑positive and HER2‑low breast cancer patients.
  • MoAs: Antibody‑drug conjugate (ADC) targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2); delivers topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (deruxtecan) after internalization, causing DNA damage and cell death. Also exhibits a bystander effect due to membrane‑permeable payload.
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma, Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: Regeneron Fianlimab Melanoma Failure
item.description:
• Summary: Regeneron's anti-LAG-3 antibody fianlimab missed its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 melanoma trial, failing to beat Merck's Keytruda and adding to setbacks for LAG-3 inhibitors.
  • MoAs: LAG-3 inhibitor
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, STAT News, Oncology Pipeline, BioSpace, Endpoints News, Fierce Biotech

item.title: Ovarian Cancer Opportunity
item.description:
• Summary: A sponsored article from Pharmaceutical Technology discusses the complexity of conducting global clinical trials for ovarian cancer. It highlights challenges in patient recruitment, regulatory variation across countries, and the need for strategic trial design to accelerate development of new therapies. The piece emphasizes the importance of partnerships and innovative approaches to overcome these hurdles and unlock opportunities in this therapeutic area.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: Revolution Pancreatic Cancer Drug
item.description:
• Summary: A BioSpace article discusses whether Revolution Medicines' experimental pancreatic cancer drug can be surpassed by new candidates from Immuneering and Actuate Therapeutics. Revolution's drug, likely a SOS1 inhibitor targeting the RAS pathway, has shown promising early data. Immuneering's IMM-1-104 and Actuate's approach aim to improve upon efficacy or tolerability. The piece highlights the growing competition in the KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer space and the need for better treatments.
  • MoAs: SOS1 inhibitor (RAS pathway inhibitor) for Revolution's drug; for Immuneering: dual MEK/ERK inhibitor; for Actuate: not specified but likely a targeted therapy
  • Sources: BioSpace
